producer_report.summary: Only one job at a time now holds a build folder, so two jobs can run at once. A second job reads and plans, then waits for the folder before its producer builds. It is not held for low disk, no attempt is used, and it is not discarded. `max_concurrency` stays 2 (the base already had it). The slot is a one-entry queue in `<state>/build-folder/`. The job takes it in `dispatch`, after planning and before the baseline checks, and frees it when the job is closed. Freeing removes the job's `target/` first, then releases the slot. At dispatch, a free-space shortfall that the holder's own measured folder explains does not hold a job. Any other shortfall holds as before. The wait is left out of `wall_time_execution`. New tests simulate free space and sample the disk for build-folder holders (peak 1 across two jobs); they pass, and the two-slot mutation made the main one fail. D188, design section 11 and a CHANGELOG entry (stopgap lifted) are added. The full athena-cli run showed one failing existing test, which I changed because the new behavior contradicts it (open_issues).

criteria_check.criterion: A new test in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs (or crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs) drains two jobs with max_concurrency = 2. It asserts that both jobs reach planning together, that the second producer starts only after the first job frees its build folder, and that the peak count of build-folder holders is 1. Both jobs land, and neither is discarded or held for low disk. Run with cargo test; the test fails if the slot gate is removed.
criteria_check.evidence: `run::tests::produce_and_verify_order_tests::build_folder::two_jobs_plan_together_and_build_one_after_the_other` (cargo test -p athena-core two_jobs_plan_together_and_build_one_after_the_other) runs two real Athena::go calls on two threads. It does not set max_concurrency: the test calls `go` directly, as the drain's workers do. A planner barrier proves both jobs are inside planning. The log is planning, planning, first-start, first-end, first-verifier, second-start, second-verifier. The second producer asserts the first job's `target` is gone. A 2 ms sampler counts jobs with a real directory under jobs/*/target/*, and the peak is 1. Neither job has a `held` line or a hold marker. One deviation: the second job ends Stale on its first `go`, because the first job's landing moved the branch. That is the existing landing rule in land.rs and has nothing to do with disk. The test retries it and it lands, so both land. Mutation check: with the queue set to 2 slots the test fails (a producer started while the other's folder existed, and no waiter appeared).

criteria_check.criterion: A test shows a job waiting for the slot does not count as a low-disk hold or discard. With a simulated free-space value below the gate while another job holds the folder, the waiting job stays queued and is later started. Run with cargo test.
criteria_check.evidence: `a_job_waiting_for_the_build_folder_is_not_held_for_low_disk`: a 12 GB simulated disk, with the first job's sparse 8 GB folder, gives 4 GB free against the 10 GB gate (asserted). The second job's `go` prints a `disk` line naming the holder, queues at the folder, then runs its producer and lands after the first job closes. It has no held line and no hold marker. The counter-test `a_job_short_of_disk_for_its_own_reasons_is_still_held_at_dispatch` has a 5 GB ballast. It still returns LowDisk (5.0 GB free), prints the held line, writes a hold marker and never runs its producer. disk.rs `the_credit_counts_only_the_slot_holder` covers the credit rule.

criteria_check.criterion: A test shows the slot is freed on every exit path (landed, rejected, failed or discarded job). A second job that was waiting then proceeds. Run with cargo test.
criteria_check.evidence: `the_build_folder_is_freed_on_every_way_a_job_ends` covers landed, rejected and failed-with-no-change. After each, `assert_folder_free` checks no ticket, the slot is takeable, the job's target is gone and the holder file is gone. Then the next job's producer runs and ends in the same state. Separate tests cover held for low disk before the producer (`the_build_folder_is_freed_when_a_job_is_held_for_low_disk_before_its_producer`, then the next job lands) and killed while waiting (`a_job_killed_while_it_waits_for_the_build_folder_leaves_no_ticket`). `a_resumed_job_takes_the_build_folder_before_its_checks` covers the resume path. The code has no discard state. disk.rs `dropping_the_build_folder_removes_the_jobs_target_and_the_holder_file_before_the_slot_is_free` and `a_second_job_waits_for_the_build_folder_until_the_first_guard_drops` cover the guard itself.

open_issues: Deviation from the plan, and from the listed deliverables: I edited crates/athena-cli/tests/lifecycle.rs. The test `a_blocked_job_keeps_its_directory_until_it_is_closed_and_closing_reports_the_exact_space` asserted that a job that ends Blocked keeps `target/debug/big`. The guard now frees the build folder on every ending, so that job no longer keeps its build cache. Keeping it would leave a 15-24 GB folder beside the next job's build, which is the fault this change fixes. The test now asserts the directory stays and `target` is gone. It plants a cache again before `close`, so the exact-space report is still checked. D188 and the CHANGELOG say so. The owner may prefer to keep the cache for a blocked job. That would need a guard that skips the removal for Blocked, and then the slot would not mean 'no folder held'.
The full `cargo test --locked` was not green on my last full run (that one lifecycle test). I fixed the test and re-ran it alone. Athena's own run on the final tree is the check.

run/mod.rs and scoring.rs are not listed deliverables but were edited: `dispatch` is where the slot must be taken, and scoring.rs holds one label string. admission.rs is a listed deliverable and is unchanged: it holds no disk or slot logic and runs before dispatch.
Nothing here measured free space on a real disk. Tests simulate it, and the drain's own rebuild and the check slots' warm directories stay outside the slot (named in D188 and section 11).

The test for criterion 1 calls `Athena::go` on two threads and does not set `max_concurrency`: the drain's `drain_concurrent` tests use a stub that never reaches the slot. The live value is checked separately by `the_live_config_allows_two_jobs_at_once`.
mistakes: I first wrote the test `two_jobs_plan_together_and_build_one_after_the_other` expecting both jobs to land on their first `go`. That fails on the existing stale rule. I fixed it by retrying the stale job, inside the same sampled window.
I first designed the notes helper around the request text ("once more"). A retry's reading needs the retried job's file as a deliverable, so it is keyed on the job id instead.
The guard's drop removing `target` broke an existing lifecycle test that pinned a blocked job's kept build cache. I found it only in the crate-wide run and changed that test (see open_issues).
learnings: The base athena.toml already read `max_concurrency = 2` at line 205. The part 1 stopgap was not in the base.

Two jobs dispatched from the same base cannot both land on their first `go`. land.rs plan() compares the fingerprint of governed content, which is everything except records/ and owner paths. The second job ends Stale, and its retry (stale merge, no producer run) lands it.

A producer is sent back once when a deliverable of the reading is unchanged. A test that gives each job its own file therefore also changes the reading's deliverable and the plan's file. A retry's reading must list the retried job's files as deliverables.

The baseline checks run for real with CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<job dir>/target/verify and no slot link, so that directory is real. Later check commands link target/verify to a check slot's warm directory for one command and remove the link afterwards.
The in-loop checks skip, with a `producer   checks not run before the verifier` line, when disk is low. They do not hold a job.
The producer's `cargo` goes through the build-slot shim, so a second cargo command waits up to 300 s for the first and exits 75.
desires: A way to read the output file of a background cargo run: the first two full runs failed with no visible failure list, so I re-ran per crate.
The build-slot wait for cargo commands (300 s) made waiting on my own background run clumsy.
